messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks. I want my fair share, and I’m not agreeing to subsidize A by selling her the house cheaply. I don’t know what B has said about needing money, so I can’t speak for her. I want this settled fairly, but there’s no rush.

Thank you. My husband and I want to buy the house at a family discount. Having a home we can afford matters to me, and I want to be financially independent. But C’s agreement is needed, and she hasn’t agreed.

Thank you. I don’t have a particular wish to keep the house, but I’d like the estate handled fairly and not rushed. If there’s money available to me, I’d hope to use it to start a dance studio; I’m not sure what amount or share is possible.
Mostly. I do want a fair share, and there’s no rush. But “rightful share” isn’t settled, and it matters that I haven’t agreed to a discounted sale to A.
That mostly fits. The family discount matters because it affects whether we can afford to buy it. I’m not sure I have more to add about memories or location.
Yes, that’s right. I’d only add that I’d like my share to give me a little more independence, if that’s possible.
Mostly. I haven’t agreed to A buying at a discount; I can’t say that every estate decision needs my consent. I don’t know what the will says or who the executor is.

Yes, that fits. I’m open to exploring options, but I’d need to understand the costs and whether they’d leave me financially secure before agreeing to anything. I still hope we can find a price that works for the family.
Yes, that fits. And yes, I’m fine with checking the will, executor, and an independent house valuation before anyone commits. There’s no rush.
I’m afraid I don’t know what the will says or who the executor is. Getting those facts and an independent valuation first sounds sensible to me.
No, that seems sensible. I’d just want to keep my finance details private unless I choose to share them.
The fact-finding is fine, as long as A exploring finance doesn’t imply I’ll accept a discount or cover any shortfall. B’s likely share should be clarified from the will and the facts, not guessed.
That seems sensible, as long as the figure for my share is only an estimate until the will and other details are clear. I’d also hope nobody feels committed just because A looks into financing.
